Multi-negative cross-entropy computes −s⁺ + log(exp(s⁺)+Σexp(s⁻)); without sampling corrections, call it sampled-candidate cross-entropy. Importance-corrected sampled softmax requires corrections matching the actual sampling design. For a deterministic positive and K distinct negatives drawn uniformly from an eligible set of size M, the negative partition estimator is (M/K)Σexp(s⁻): equivalently, add log(M/K) to negative logits, leaving the positive unchanged. This derivation uses inclusion probability K/M; subtracting the same uniform correction from every candidate cancels and does not implement it. An unbiased partition estimate still generally produces biased finite-sample loss/gradients. Sources: [TensorFlow sampling definitions](https://www.tensorflow.org/extras/candidate_sampling.pdf), [sampled-softmax analysis](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v80/blanc18a/blanc18a.pdf).

Implementation implications: define each user's eligible set from catalog IDs excluding padding, training positives and the current target; sample Kᵤ=min(K,Mᵤ) without replacement and use each row's Mᵤ/Kᵤ correction. Excluding training positives changes support: this estimates a denominator over the positive plus eligible items, not unrestricted full-catalog softmax. Mask unused candidate slots to −∞; handle empty eligible sets explicitly. Duplicate negatives otherwise repeat denominator mass; deduplication changes the sampling design and requires matching inclusion probabilities. Average one loss per valid prediction position, excluding padding; do not divide cross-entropy again by negative count. PyTorch documents [cross-entropy reduction](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.CrossEntropyLoss.html). These are implementation deductions from the sampling definitions.

Filtering known positives prevents known collisions but cannot establish that unobserved items are true negatives. Sampling-probability correction and false-negative correction address separate problems; never consult held-out labels to filter training negatives. [Research on implicit-feedback false negatives](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.15973) explains the remaining ambiguity.
